jamninkaornis:study:1.title: A new passerine (Aves: Passeriformes) and three other specimens of Late Oligocene birds from Poland, with a review of all Paleogene birds from the northern part of the Carpathian Arc (Palaeontologia Electronica, 2026)

facts.statement: Jamninkaornis is classified as a passerine bird belonging to the suborder Tyranni.
facts.quote: A passerine in the suborder Tyranni.

facts.statement: The genus Jamninkaornis contains only one known species, Jamninkaornis kencampbelli.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Jamninkaornis kencampbelli

facts.statement: The species is known from a single coracoid and humerus, which are pectoral and forelimb bones.
facts.quote: known from a single coracoid and humerus (pectoral and forelimb bones)

facts.statement: The specimen consists of a right coracoid and humerus preserved on two separate rock slabs.
facts.quote: consists of a right coracoid (pectoral girdle bone) and humerus (upper forelimb bone), preserved on two separate slabs of rock

facts.statement: Jamninkaornis kencampbelli was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Zbigniew M. Bochenski and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Zbigniew M. Bochenski and colleagues described Jamninkaornis kencampbelli as a new genus and species of passerine bird

facts.statement: The genus name Jamninkaornis combines the name of a local stream and valley with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name, Jamninkaornis, combines a reference to Jamninka, a stream and valley close to the type locality, with the Greek word ὄρνῑς (órnīs), meaning bird

facts.statement: Jamninkaornis lived during the Oligocene epoch.
The fossil range of Jamninkaornis is the Late Oligocene (Chattian).
Jamninkaornis is known from the late Oligocene (Chattian age), approximately 26 million years ago, in Poland.
facts.quote: known from the late Oligocene (Chattian age, 26 million years ago) of Poland
